task: r3t3 - review t2: is the guard actually wired into the flow, is it paste-runnable, and was any runbook content deleted
overallVerdict: partial - 7 of 8 criteria hold, criterion 2 (wiring position) fails as written: the guard's own precondition tells the operator to bind the landing tab first and run the guard afterwards
headline: The guard is real, it is wired in front of the visibility probe, and it works when pasted. On the live editor page the runbook's own JS block returns JS_FAILED with `Error: WRONG_PAGE: https://pro.lceda.cn/editor#id=... is not http://127.0.0.1:49620/landing` and dpx exits 1; on a real landing page the same block returns status ok with url = the landing URL and exits 0; and with $RelayPort set to 49621 against that 49620 landing it throws `... is not http://127.0.0.1:49621/landing`, which is the test that distinguishes real parameterization from a hardcoded port. Nothing protected was deleted: every count I compared is equal or higher and the timeline table still has its 10 data rows. t2 also really did run both negatives, recorded in r10t7 at 14:53:42.664Z (unbound) and 14:56:10.070Z (after switching back to the editor). What fails is the placement rule: section 3.0's 执行前置 says to tab-select the landing page first and run the guard after, which is the after-binding order the dispatch says must fail. That choice is documented and defensible - the author ran the guard unbound first, saw it throw because section 2's tab-new does not activate the created tab, and then wrote the runbook to bind first - but as written the guard's remaining job is to catch a select that silently failed, not to keep the probe off the editor page.

findings.detail: at HEAD a1eac6b the runbook had no 3.0 and r10t7 did not exist; 27408b7 added both while I was reviewing. I re-verified everything against 27408b7 and kept the earlier reading in the headDrift block rather than deleting it.

findings.title: the guard is documented to run after the tab-select binding
findings.detail: L129 tells the operator to select the landing tab first. That is the after-binding placement the dispatch rejects. The author's reason is measured and documented in r10t7 (tab-new does not activate the tab), but the consequence is that the guard now only guards against a failed select.

findings.title: the JS block loses its failure in the wrapper's exit code
findings.detail: dpx exits 1 on WRONG_PAGE, but a .ps1 whose last line is `dpx eval $js` exits 0. Measured 1 / 0 / 1 for dpx direct, no exit, and exit $LASTEXITCODE.

findings.title: r10t7 quotes blocks that are not the runbook's blocks
findings.detail: r10t7.runbook.guardBody equals the runbook JS block plus one line ($RelayPort = 49620), and r10t7.runbook.psGuardBody documents a usage-example variant while the runbook carries the 正例/负例 form with $editorUrl. Neither quote is byte-identical to what an operator copies, and guardBody contradicts r10t7's own claim of 'no literal 49620 in the runbook guard code'. The runbook text itself is fine - I executed it and it works - but the evidence artifact points at different text.

findings.title: the PS block cannot serve as a gate
findings.detail: it prints PASS and then throws on the editor URL, so pasting it verbatim always ends with WRONG_PAGE.

findings.title: my first 49621 attempt was invalid and I discarded it
findings.detail: I built the header with a double-quoted PowerShell string, so $RelayPort expanded to empty and the page received `const RELAY_PORT = ;`, producing a SyntaxError instead of WRONG_PAGE. I rebuilt it with a literal and re-ran; only the corrected run is reported.
